result:
March US accruals are booked. Summary of what I did and why:

**Posted — total USD 21,600 to 2100 Accrued Expenses**

| Entry | Vendor | Amount | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| JE-00304 | Juniper Data Consulting | 7,350.00 | Posted |
| JE-00305 | Parker & Rowe LLP | 14,250.00 | Pending approval |

- **Juniper (Dr 6520 / Cr 2100):** 42.0 approved hours × $175/hr per SOW 2026-02. Supported by the approved March timesheet (DOC-0204) and the SOW (DOC-0074). Billed monthly in arrears, invoice comes in April — textbook unbilled-services accrual. Under the $10k limit, so no approval needed.
- **Parker & Rowe (Dr 6500 / Cr 2100):** Vendor's written confirmation of $14,250 of time recorded through 3/31 (DOC-0209). Work was performed in March, invoice issues 4/10.

**Approval policy followed:** JE-00305 exceeds the USD 10,000 senior accountant posting limit (Policy §1), so I routed it to the Controller via `request_approval` immediately after posting. It sits in `pending_approval` until they act. I kept the two vendors as separate entries — that's two distinct obligations, not threshold-splitting, which the policy prohibits.

**Deliberately not accrued:** The Brightline Media $11,000 April campaign (DOC-0197). It's an unsigned quote, work starts April 6, and nothing was received in March — Policy §5 says proposals for future work aren't liabilities. Rather than silently dropping it, I logged it as EXC-001 so the Controller can confirm.

**One thing worth your attention:** account 2100 carried a pre-existing USD 38,200 credit balance that traces entirely to JE-00013, the 1/1/26 opening-balance migration, with zero movement all quarter and no supporting documentation. It doesn't affect the March accruals or create any double-count risk, so I left it alone rather than forcing an adjustment — but a balance that hasn't moved in three months and has no support behind it is worth confirming is still a valid obligation.

I set **AP cutoff review** to `in_progress` rather than complete — it shouldn't close until JE-00305 is approved and someone sweeps early-April invoices for March service periods, which I did not do. "Accrue unpaid payroll" was out of scope and remains open.
